text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Electronic signals from audio surveillance equipment detected in conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz's house.
- Japanese credit agency JCR downgrades Turkey's credit rating from BB+ to BB.
- Islamist-led government trying to lead Turkey to a closed regime with plans to censor the press.
- State security court retrial of 42 Islamists charged with arson killing of 37 people in 1993 begins.
- Conflicting reports on whereabouts of government MP involved in car crash scandal that exposed links between the police and organised crime.
- Some 50,000 people queued up for five days to apply for 2,500 vacant positions in Social Insurance Authority.
- Turkish lira has lost 1,427 times its value against U.S. dollar in past 16 years.
- Car producer TOFAS workers temporarily laid off.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan calls on intelligence service to investigate the car crash scandal.
- Conscientious objector Murat Ulke released by court but still ordered to do his military service.
